# Involutions

*The self-inverse permutations of $[n]$ — those equal to their own inverse ($\sigma = \sigma^{-1}$).*

## Usage

| Form | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $\operatorname{Involutions}(n)$ | all involutions of $[n]$ (fixed points + disjoint transpositions) |
| $\operatorname{At}(\operatorname{Involutions}(n),\ i)$ | the involution at 1-based position $i$ |

## Details

- **Arity:** 1 — the ground size $n$.
- **Element:** a permutation (one-line) built only from fixed points and 2-cycles. `[2, 1, 3, 4]` swaps $1 \leftrightarrow 2$ and fixes $3, 4$.
- **Result type:** `collection` of `list<integer>`, each of length $n$.
- **Count:** the involution / telephone numbers $I(n)$ (OEIS [A000085](https://oeis.org/A000085): $1, 1, 2, 4, 10, 26, \dots$), satisfying $I(n) = I(n-1) + (n-1)\,I(n-2)$ (`InvolutionCount`).
- **Order:** recursion on the last label $n$: either it is fixed (the first $I(n-1)$ ranks) or paired with label $j$ (`InvolutionUnrank`/`Rank`).
- **Random access:** $O(n)$ with a memoized telephone-number table.

## Examples

$\operatorname{Count}(\operatorname{Involutions}(4)) = 10$

The 10 involutions of $[4]$ in rank order are $[1, 2, 3, 4], [2, 1, 3, 4], [3, 2, 1, 4], [1, 3, 2, 4], [4, 2, 3, 1], [4, 3, 2, 1], [1, 4, 3, 2], [3, 4, 1, 2], [1, 2, 4, 3], [2, 1, 4, 3]$ — rank $0$ is the identity $[1, 2, 3, 4]$; $[2, 1, 3, 4]$ is the single transposition $(1\,2)$.
